questions.question: Which line of Python code correctly prints the text "Hellow" to the console?

options.text: print("Hellow")
Print(Hellow)
output "Hellow"
echo << "Hellow"

questions.explanation_correct:
EXCELLENT!
Python's print() function is lowercase, followed by parentheses and quotation marks around the text.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Not quite!
Python is case-sensitive, so print must be lowercase with parentheses and quotation marks around text: print("Hellow").

questions.question: What is the crucial difference between print(5) and print("5")?
questions.code:
print(5)    # Case A
print("5")  # Case B

options.text: 5 is a numeric integer (int) ready for math, while "5" is a text string (str).
print(5) causes an immediate error because numbers cannot be printed.
print("5") prints five blank lines.
There is zero difference under the hood in Python memory.

questions.explanation_correct:
SPOT ON!
Numbers without quotes are stored as integers (int), allowing arithmetic. Text in quotes is treated as string (str).
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Try Again!
5 without quotes is an integer (int); "5" in quotes is text (str). While they look similar when printed, their types in memory are completely different!

questions.question: Why will Python report a SyntaxError for this code?

options.text: The opening quote was not closed before the parenthesis (unterminated string).
The word "Hellow" is not a recognized Python keyword.
Python only allows single quotes, never double quotes.
print() cannot be used on the first line of a script.

questions.explanation_correct:
NICE!
Every opening quotation mark must have a matching closing quotation mark before the closing parenthesis.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Not quite!
Quotes must always come in matching pairs (start and end). Missing the closing quote creates an unterminated string literal error.

questions.question: Which statement will output the character sequence P Y T H O N?
questions.code: # Target: P Y T H O N

options.text: print("P Y T H O N")
print(P, Y, T, H, O, N)
sequence["P Y T H O N"]
letter_display(P-Y-T-H-O-N)

questions.explanation_correct:
WELL DONE!
Writing the text sequence inside quotation marks inside print() will cleanly display 'P Y T H O N' in the console.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Try Again!
Without quotes, Python thinks P, Y, T, etc., are variable names. Wrapping them in quotes print("P Y T H O N") prints the characters as text.

questions.question: What happens if you write print(Hellow) without quotes?

options.text: Python thinks Hellow is a variable name and raises a NameError: name 'Hellow' is not defined.
Python automatically adds quotes and prints it normally.
Python translates it into another language.
The computer reboots.

questions.explanation_correct:
MODULE COMPLETE!
Without quotes, Python looks for an existing variable named Hellow. If no such variable was created, it throws a NameError.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
Almost!
Any word written without quotation marks is assumed to be a variable or keyword. Without prior assignment, it raises a NameError.
